properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued June 3 at 11:33AM CDT until June 3 at 2:30PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Culberson County in southwestern Texas...
North Central Jeff Davis County in southwestern Texas...
Reeves County in southwestern Texas...
West Central Ward County in western Texas...

* Until 230 PM CDT /130 PM MDT/.

* At 1133 AM CDT /1033 AM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 1 inch of rain
has fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Pecos, Kent, Toyah, Balmorhea, Barstow, Saragosa, Balmorhea State
Park, Balmorhea Lake, Verhalen, Toyahvale, Pecos Municipal Airport
and Toyah Lake.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.
properties.area: Culberson, TX; Jeff Davis, TX; Reeves, TX; Ward, TX

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued June 3 at 10:34AM CDT until June 3 at 12:30PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Aransas County in south central Texas...

* WHEN...Until 1230 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1034 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 2 and 3.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northeastern Aransas County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued June 3 at 9:19AM CDT until June 7 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Arkansas...

Cache River Near Patterson affecting Jackson and Woodruff
Counties.

For the Cache River...including Patterson...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Cache River near Patterson.

* WHEN...Until Monday morning

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Pastureland and cropland not protected by
levees in Jackson and Woodruff counties affected. Water is over
portions of State Highway 37 and deep along the shoulders of State
Highway 18 near Grubbs. Water over portions of Woodruff County
Road 775 north of State Highway 260.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 9.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
early Saturday afternoon and continue falling to 8.3 feet
Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

River forecasts are based on current conditions and rainfall
forecasted to occur over the next 24 hours. During periods of
flooding...Evening forecasts are reissued with updated rainfall
forecasts.

Observed and forecasted stage data plots are available on our
Advanced Hydrologic Prediction Service web page at...
www.weather.gov/lzk

Under the Current Conditions section...Select River and Lakes AHPS.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday evening around
7:45pmThursday morning at 930 AM CDT.

forecast.

* WHERE...Osage River at Taberville.

* WHEN...Until late tomorrow evening.

* IMPACTS...At 23.3 feet, The handicapped access to the Osage River
launch near Taberville floods.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM CDT Wednesday the stage was 23.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 23.0 feet.

tomorrow afternoon.

23.2 feet on 06/21/2013.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued June 2 at 12:07PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Stehekin River at Stehekin affecting Chelan County.

For the Stehekin River...including Stehekin...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and forecast to continue.

* WHERE...Stehekin River at Stehekin.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 20.5 feet, water inundates some properties and
overtops the temporary corduroy bridge. Company Creek Road
inundated at northern end. Battalion Creek culverts are beginning
to be overtopped. Water begins damaging Wood Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM PDT Tuesday the stage was 20.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 19.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 11:30 AM PDT Tuesday was 21.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.5
feet early Thursday morning.  The river is currently forecast
to briefly drop below flood stage by a couple inches early
next week, before again rising above flood stage.
- Flood stage is 20.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
22.5 feet on 05/12/2019.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive
cars through flooded areas.

This warning will be in effect until the river falls below its flood
stage.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at 1245 PM PDT.
